title: Indus River System
definition: The Indus River System is one of the world's major transboundary river basins, originating in the Tibetan Plateau, flowing through India and Pakistan, and draining into the Arabian Sea. It encompasses the mighty Indus River along with its major Himalayan and trans-Himalayan tributaries.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for Geography (Drainage System, Physiography, Himalayan rivers vs Peninsular rivers) in Prelims, and International Relations / Geopolitics (Indus Waters Treaty, hydro-diplomacy) in Mains GS-2.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Indus River System.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic physiography of Northern India and Tibet
